Content: Students in Africa, Australia, and North America each dropped a `text(10-gram)` bag of sand to determine the behavior of the sandbag. `text(Each bag)` of sand fell straight down to the ground. The table shows additional data the students collected for their sandbag investigation.
problems/TN25G5S/media/1a.jpg
Based on the information, which statement `ultext(best)` explains the behavior of the sandbag at `text(each location)`?

A.Choice: Gravity pushes objects toward the center of `text(Earth)` at the same speed in the same amount of time.

B.Choice: Gravity pulls objects of the same mass toward the center of `text(Earth)` in the same way.

C.Choice: Gravity acts differently on objects that appear different from `text(one)` another.

D.Choice: Gravity acts differently on objects that are at different temperatures.

Content: The table shows the sizes and types of galaxies that can be found in the universe. A `text(light-year)` is the distance it takes light to travel in `text(one year)`.
problems/TN25G5S/media/2a.jpg
Which `ultext(two)` statements `ultext(best)` compare the relationships between the Milky Way galaxy with the other galaxies listed in the table?

A.Choice: Galaxy `text(Y)` is closer to `text(Earth)` than the Milky Way galaxy, and its stars are arranged together at its center like the Milky Way galaxy.

B.Choice: The stars in Galaxy `text(X)` and Galaxy `text(W)` are arranged into arms that rotate around the galaxy's center like the Milky Way galaxy.

C.Choice: Galaxy `text(W)` is similar in size to the Milky Way galaxy, and Galaxy `text(W)` is farther from `text(Earth)` than the Milky Way galaxy.

D.Choice: The stars in Galaxy `text(Y)` and Galaxy `text(Z)` are arranged in a similar way as the stars in the Milky Way galaxy.

E.Choice: Both Galaxy `text(W)` and Galaxy `text(X)` are similar in size to the Milky Way galaxy.

Content: The table shows information that scientists collected about green sea turtle hatchlings that came from `text(three)` different nests. `text(Each nest)` had `100` green sea turtle eggs and had a different typical temperature. Temperature was measured in `text(degrees Celsius)` (`°text(C)`).
problems/TN25G5S/media/3a.jpg
Which characteristic of green sea turtle hatchlings was `ultext(most)` affected by their interaction with the environment?

D.Choice: the number of hatchlings with hard shells

Content: The table shows data some scientists collected about `text(two)` groups of young lemon sharks between `1998` and `1999`. Length was measured in `text(centimeters)` (`text(cm)`) and mass was measured in `text(kilograms)` (`text(kg)`).
problems/TN25G5S/media/4a.jpg

The scientists claim that smaller lemon sharks are more likely to survive than larger lemon sharks. Which `ultext(three)` pieces of evidence from the table `ultext(best)` support the scientists' claim?

A.Choice: In both `text(years)`, Group `1` sharks were smaller and had a higher survival rate than Group `2` sharks.

B.Choice: In `text(each year)`, more Group `2` sharks had a shorter typical length and had a lower mass than the Group `1` sharks.

C.Choice: Group `2` sharks in `1998` had a shorter typical length and had a higher survival rate than Group `2` sharks in `1999`.

D.Choice: Group `1` sharks in `1999` had a lower mass and had a higher survival rate than Group `1` sharks in `1998`.

E.Choice: Group `1` and Group `2` had higher survival rates in `1998` compared to `1999`.

Content: The table shows data for a student who rode a sled down different snow-covered hills. Hill height was measured in `text(meters)` (`text(m)`) and sled speed was measured in `text(meters per second)` (`text(m)//text(s)`).
problems/TN25G5S/media/5a.jpg
Based on the data in the table, at which speed was the sled `ultext(most likely)` going down Hill `text(Z)`?
Students want to determine whether mixing `text(two)` powdered solids creates a change in the properties of those substances. The teacher shows the students a demonstration:

:ibox:• The teacher places a wooden block on the table and pours a small amount of water on the block.

• Then the teacher takes a beaker and places it on the wet wooden block.

• The teacher mixes `text(two)` powdered solid substances in the beaker, forming a mixture.

• After `30` `text(seconds)`, the teacher lifts the beaker, and the wooden block is frozen to the bottom of the beaker.
The figure shows the demonstration before and after the powdered solids are mixed.
`ultext(Mixing Powdered Solids Demonstration)`
problems/TN25G5S/media/6a.jpg
problems/TN25G5S/media/6b.jpg
The table shows the properties of the substances and the mixture. Temperature is measured in `text(degrees Celsius)` (`°text(C)`).
problems/TN25G5S/media/6c.jpg
Based on the data, which `ultext(two)` pieces of evidence support the claim that the properties of the `text(two)` substances changed?

A.Choice: The mass increased by the end of the investigation.

B.Choice: The temperature decreased by the end of the investigation.

C.Choice: Substance `1` and Substance `2` were solids that formed a liquid after mixing.

D.Choice: The mass of the `text(two)` solids is equal to the mass of the liquid.

E.Choice: The temperature of `text(each solid)` was `24°text(C)` in the beaker.

Content: As `text(Earth)` revolves around the `text(Sun)`, different parts of the planet experience different seasons. The figure shows where the country of Brazil is located on `text(Earth)` as well as the movement of `text(Earth)` around the `text(Sun)`.
problems/TN25G5S/media/8a.jpg
Based on the model, which season does Brazil experience during `text(June)`?

B.Choice: `text(spring)`, because rays of light from the `text(Sun)` travel in straight lines

C.Choice: `text(summer)`, because there is more daylight than darkness during this time

D.Choice: `text(winter)`, because that portion of `text(Earth)` is tilted away from the `text(Sun)`

Content: Based on the information in Table `2` (Part `1`), what should the mass of the milk and vinegar be after these substances are combined?
A student claims that the lumps in the milk and vinegar mixture cause the mass of the mixture to be greater than the total mass of the substances before mixing.
Based on the information in Table `2` (Part `1`), which statement `ultext(best)` evaluates the claim?

A.Choice: The claim is incorrect because the lumps are just a rearrangement of matter that was already present.

B.Choice: The claim is incorrect because when the vinegar disappears, the combined mass is less than what was measured.

C.Choice: The claim is correct because the matter in the lumps is closer together than the matter in the liquid.

D.Choice: The claim is correct because when the materials change phase, there is an increase in the combined mass.

Content: Based on the information in Table `1` (Part `1`), which statement `ultext(best)` explains why the mass of the water and sugar mixture is `104` `text(grams)`?

A.Choice: The sugar combined with water to make a new substance at the bottom of the bottle.

B.Choice: The sugar reacted with water to create a new gas that left the bottle.

C.Choice: The sugar is no longer in the bottle because it cannot be seen.

D.Choice: The sugar is still in the bottle even though it cannot be seen.

Content: Based on the information in Table `3` (Part `2`), what was the mass of the tablet used in the water and tablet investigation?
A student claims that the mixing of `text(two)` substances may not produce a new substance. Based on the information in Part `2`, which evidence `ultext(best)` supports the student's claim?

A.Choice: Before the cap was removed in the investigation in Table `3`, the mass of the mixture was equal to the mass of the water and the tablet.

B.Choice: After the cap was removed in the investigation in Table `3`, the mass of the mixture decreased by `1` `text(gram)` as gas left the bottle.

C.Choice: Before the substances were mixed in the investigation in Table `4`, the water was a clear liquid and the sand was brown, tan, and beige grains.

D.Choice: After the substances were mixed in the investigation in Table `4`, the initial properties of the water and sand stayed the same.

Content: A student demonstrates an activity by completing these steps:

:ibox:`1`. The student places drawings of different constellations on the walls of the classroom.

`2`. The student stands in the middle of the classroom and spins slowly.

`3`. The student observes how the constellations appear to move as the student spins.
Which statement `ultext(best)` describes what the student is modeling with this activity?

A.Choice: As `text(Earth)` revolves around the constellations, the constellations appear to move across the sky.

B.Choice: As constellations revolve around `text(Earth)`, the positions of the constellations in the sky change.

C.Choice: `text(Earth's)` rotation makes the constellations appear to move around `text(Earth)`.

D.Choice: Constellations move at the same speed that `text(Earth)` rotates on its axis.

Content: Scientists noticed that wolves of the same species have different fur colors. The scientists observed the fur colors of `text(two)` generations of wolves living among other wolves in Yellowstone National Park. The scientists' data are shown in the table.
problems/TN25G5S/media/17a.jpg
Which statement about how wolves pass on fur color to offspring is `ultext(best)` supported by the data?

A.Choice: Wolves with either fur color are more likely to have offspring with gray fur.

B.Choice: Wolves with either fur color can produce offspring with either color of fur.

C.Choice: Female wolves with gray fur are less likely to have offspring with black fur.

D.Choice: Male wolves with black fur are less likely to have offspring with black fur.

Content: The figure shows changes that occur in a substance in a sealed container.

Which statement `ultext(best)` explains why the changes to the substance occurred?

A.Choice: A gas turned into a liquid because energy was removed from the particles.

B.Choice: A gas turned into a liquid because the particles absorbed energy.

C.Choice: A solid turned into a liquid because energy was removed from the particles.
